title: Account brief
blurb: What they told us, who we know, open deals and who is missing

search.question: Brief me on {account}: why they talk to us in their own words, who we have spoken with there by seniority and when each last spoke, their open deals, who we have never reached, and the three things to raise next.

title: Call prep and follow-ups
blurb: A one-page brief and two follow-up drafts, ready before the call

search.question: Prep me for my call with {account}: what they care about, who we know there by seniority, which deals are open, three things to raise, and the two likely objections with the answer that worked with other buyers.

title: QBR and renewal prep
blurb: A one-page review: value delivered, risks, people and next asks

search.question: Prep my QBR with {account}: why they bought in their own words and whether later calls show we delivered it, wins and complaints since then, who we reach now compared with before they signed, risks to the renewal, and the two expansion asks with the best evidence.

title: Expansion signals
blurb: Customers showing signs they will buy more, ranked, with quotes

search.question: Which current customers showed expansion signals in the last 90 days, such as new teams or regions, pain a product they do not own solves, more senior people on calls, budget timing or a renewal coming up? Rank them, with a quote for each.

title: Early churn warnings
blurb: Customers at risk, why, and whether anyone has responded

search.question: Which current customers show early churn risk, such as a stalled rollout, a workaround, questions about price or contract terms, a competitor named or a champion leaving, and did our side respond?

title: Whitespace by account
blurb: What each customer could still buy, and the pain behind each gap

search.question: Which current customers describe a need that {products} would meet, and have they bought it? Give the strongest quote for each gap.

title: Asked for, never sold
blurb: What customers asked for that no deal followed

search.question: What have our customers asked for that we never sold them? Group the asks by how many accounts raised them, with their words and dates.

title: Stalled deal review
blurb: Open deals gone quiet, what was last said, and a next step

search.question: Which open deals have had no conversation with the buyer in 30 days or are past their close date, and what did the buyer say last?

title: Why we lose deals
blurb: Lost deals grouped by what killed them, and what would have helped

search.question: Why do we lose deals? Group our closed-lost deals from the last two quarters by what killed them, and name the proof that would have answered each group.

title: At-risk open deals
blurb: Open deals rated at risk, and the one constraint holding each back

search.question: Which open deals are rated at risk, and what is the one constraint holding each back?

title: Champions gone quiet
blurb: Champions on big open deals who went silent, and their last words

search.question: Which champions on open deals over $50,000 have gone quiet in the last 30 days, and what was the last thing each one said?

title: Competitors in buyer words
blurb: Who buyers name, why we win or lose, and quotes for each

search.question: Which competitors and alternatives do buyers name on calls, and why do we win or lose against each one?

title: Positioning vs buyer words
blurb: Where our messages match how buyers talk, and where they do not

search.question: Compare these messages with how buyers describe the problem in their own words: {messages}. Where do buyers use our words, and what do they keep raising that we never say?

fills.label: Your messages
fills.example: Ship in days, not months. One price for every seat.

title: Objection answers that work
blurb: How buyers raise an objection, and the answers that moved deals

search.question: How do buyers raise {objection}, how do executives put it differently from managers, and which of our answers came before deals moved forward?
